scope: All 54 open Dependabot alerts returned by the GitHub API, plus three GitPython advisories found through PyPI. This is an audit; dependency upgrades were resolved only in scratch copies.

alerts.assessment: Calls to python-multipart parse_form with an unvalidated negative Content-Length. Starlette uses a different parser API.
A wheel includes affected OpenSSL. The maintainer identifies CVE-2026-34180, which needs an attacker-controlled ASN.1 element larger than 2 GB; Prefect uses Fernet in the inspected code.
An ASGI server must forward a malformed path without a leading slash, and application middleware must trust the resulting URL hostname.
A running service must parse attacker-controlled URL-encoded forms. Streamlit has an upload route that calls request.form after session and XSRF checks.
Loading an untrusted VCR YAML cassette invokes arbitrary Python constructors. No VCR imports or cassette calls were found in the scanned application or tests.
Requires exposed LangSmith TracingMiddleware and trace-read access to the destination workspace. No such middleware was found in the scanned code.
Requires NestedSecretsSettingsSource, nested subdirectories, and attacker-writable secrets entries. Bubble uses BaseSettings with an env file and does not configure this source.
Requires execution of the affected torch.jit.script path with malicious input. No direct TorchScript calls were found in the scanned application or inspected Docling sources.
Opening a crafted EPS image can loop before image decoding. The current Docling HTML configuration disables image fetching; other image-conversion paths require review before use.

alerts.issue: McIdas mmap read outside image buffer
alerts.assessment: Requires opening a crafted McIdas image from a filesystem path and accessing its pixels. BytesIO image handling does not use this mmap path.
Requires loading an untrusted PCF bitmap font. Image.open does not invoke this font loader; no matching loader use was found in inspected callers.
Requires compiling or exporting an untrusted PCF/BDF bitmap font. No matching operation was found in inspected callers.
Requires loading an untrusted BDF bitmap font with attacker-controlled glyph dimensions. No matching operation was found in inspected callers.
Requires the dedicated GdImageFile loader followed by decoding. No matching loader use was found in inspected callers.
Requires WindowsViewer and an attacker-controlled shell path. The observed host is macOS and the CI runner is Ubuntu; no image viewer calls were found.
Requires attacker-controlled filter sizes near integer limits. No rank filter use was found in inspected application or Docling callers.
Requires saving a one-bit image with TGA RLE encoding. No matching encoder use was found in inspected callers.
Requires extreme attacker-controlled crop, paste, or compositing coordinates. Docling performs image operations, but an end-to-end path for these extreme values was not demonstrated.
Requires Pillow PdfParser to decode untrusted compressed streams. Docling PDF handling must not be equated with use of Pillow PdfParser; no matching caller was found in inspected sources.
Requires decoding an untrusted tiled JPEG2000 image. Current HTML extraction disables image fetching; alternate image/document inputs could expose the decoder.
Requires attacker control over output image modes or ImageCms transform parameters. No matching ImageCms use was found in inspected callers.
Requires setuptools source-distribution builds on a normalization-sensitive filesystem with non-ASCII excluded files. Bubble declares Hatchling as its build backend.

alerts.issue: Joined short clone options bypass guards
alerts.assessment: Requires forwarding attacker-controlled multi_options into GitPython cloning. Streamlit does not expose such a call in the inspected source.
Requires attacker-controlled keyword names for Git operations. Inspected Streamlit calls use fixed argument names.
Requires attacker-controlled Git options or revisions reaching archive, ls_remote, iter_commits, or blame. Streamlit reads local branch names; visitor control was not found.
Requires cloning a caller-controlled URL through GitPython. No such operation was found in the application or Streamlit git utility.
Requires untrusted section names or submodule initialization from a malicious repository. No such operation was found in the inspected callers.

alerts.issue: Clone template can install executable hooks
alerts.assessment: Requires untrusted clone options and an attacker-controlled hook directory. No such operation was found in the inspected callers.
Requires attacker-controlled diff options or revision values. Streamlit calls index.diff(None) without these options.
Requires forwarding attacker-controlled Git keyword values. No such interface was found in the inspected callers.
Requires creating a remote from an attacker-controlled URL and subsequently using it. Streamlit only reads the configured remotes in the inspected source.

alerts.issue: Checkout or tag options access arbitrary files
alerts.assessment: Requires attacker-controlled checkout or tag options. No matching operation was found in the inspected callers.
Requires forwarding attacker-controlled archive options. No matching operation was found in the inspected callers.
Requires attacker-controlled Commit.count keyword arguments. No matching operation was found in the inspected callers.
Requires an aiohttp WebSocket client talking to a malicious peer. Instructor uses aiohttp in its usage CLI; no WebSocket client was found there.
Requires an aiohttp HTTP server. The inspected dependency use is a client in Instructor, not an aiohttp server.

alerts.issue: Malformed HTTP response reads heap memory
alerts.assessment: Requires the aiohttp C client parser and a malformed response. Instructor usage CLI uses this client; Bubble extraction selects SDK clients using HTTPX.
Requires a service decrypting untrusted EnvelopedData and exposing repeated distinguishable results. No matching operation was found in Bubble or Prefect; the inspected Prefect code uses Fernet.
Requires an HTTP2 request receiver or a proxy that downgrades requests. The dependency path is HTTPX client use; no H2 server or gateway was found.
Requires attacker-controlled tree revisions reaching index creation, reset, or merge. No matching operation was found in inspected callers.
Requires attacker-controlled initialization options and a prepared hook directory. No matching operation was found in inspected callers.
Requires attacker-controlled options for index removal or branch checkout. No matching operation was found in inspected callers.
Requires forwarding an attacker-controlled keyword dictionary, including the argument-splitting control. No matching interface was found.
Requires attacker-controlled configuration option names written through GitPython. No GitPython configuration writer was found in Bubble or Streamlit.
Requires initializing submodules from an attacker-controlled repository. No such operation was found in inspected callers.

Requires downloading malicious chat-template names and then saving the tokenizer or processor. Docling loads processors; no save_pretrained call was found in the inspected application or Docling sources.
Requires cryptography certificate-chain verification with constrained issuers and wildcard leaf names. Prefect uses Fernet; HTTPX TLS is not automatically this verifier.
Requires cryptography certificate-chain verification on attacker-controlled duplicate intermediates. No matching verifier was found in Bubble or Prefect.

alerts.issue: Checkpoint shard paths escape their directory
alerts.assessment: Requires loading an attacker-controlled sharded checkpoint through Accelerate. Docling brings this model stack into the environment. Version 1.15.0 still joins unvalidated weight_map paths; no patched release is established here.
Requires an untrusted .gitmodules file and a GitPython submodule read. Streamlit git_util does not access submodules in the inspected source.

Requires an attacker-influenced Git config and a GitPython write. A synthetic config reproduced the injection in 3.1.50 and remained intact in 3.1.62. No matching writer was found in application or Streamlit code.
Requires forwarding attacker-controlled blame revisions or options. No matching operation was found in inspected callers.

alerts.issue: Clone options redirect Git metadata writes
alerts.assessment: Requires attacker-controlled separate_git_dir clone options. No matching operation was found in inspected callers.

alerts.issue: Tag reference bypass reads local files
alerts.assessment: Requires an attacker-controlled positional tag reference. No matching operation was found in inspected callers.

gitpython.assessment: Streamlit opens the local repository and reads metadata. Its inspected git utility does not write config, create tags, clone repositories, or initialize submodules. These are installed vulnerabilities with conditional exposure, not evidence of a compromise.

starlette.assessment: The strongest identified network-facing path is Streamlit upload handling. The route calls request.form after checking XSRF and an active session. No listener was found on local ports 8501 or 4200 during the audit; deployments on other hosts or ports were not inspected.

pillow.assessment: Pillow is used by Docling and Streamlit. Bubble converts the primary filing HTML with the default converter. In Docling 2.96.0, HTML image fetching is false by default and the backend returns placeholders before Image.open. Arbitrary document formats, image operations, and model assets need their own runtime coverage.

vcrpy.assessment: Declared in development dependencies and installed by CI. Static inspection found no VCR imports, cassette calls, or cassette fixtures in the tested source tree. The unsafe loader is real and was reproduced using a harmless Python string constructor.

accelerate.assessment: Transitive dependency of Docling. The advisory has no first patched version. The 1.15.0 wheel retains the unchecked join and passes resulting paths to load_state_dict. Both runtime probes timed out after 90 seconds before producing a result, so the finding about 1.15.0 is based on source inspection.

aiohttp.assessment: Instructor imports aiohttp in its usage CLI. Bubble extraction selects the Anthropic/OpenAI SDK integrations, whose lockfile dependency path uses HTTPX. No direct aiohttp server or WebSocket path was found in the inspected code.

cryptography.assessment: Prefect depends on cryptography. The inspected Prefect code uses Fernet for stored-data encryption. It does not call the certificate verifier or PKCS7 APIs identified by these alerts. A vulnerable wheel remains installed.

h2.assessment: Reached through HTTPX HTTP2 support. The reported vulnerability concerns accepting and forwarding duplicate request headers in a server/proxy role. No such role was found in the application sources.

langsmith.assessment: Installed both through LangChain and the llm extra. The LangGraph flow builds a graph; no LangSmith TracingMiddleware integration was found in the application source.

pydantic-settings.assessment: Direct dependency. Bubble configures env-file loading, not the vulnerable nested-secret directory source. No explicit NestedSecretsSettingsSource call was found in the inspected code.

python-multipart.assessment: Streamlit dependency. Its upload route delegates to Starlette request.form. The advisory explicitly distinguishes this from the vulnerable direct parse_form convenience function.

setuptools.assessment: Transitive through Torch. The vulnerability concerns producing source archives; Bubble specifies Hatchling. This is not a runtime network exploit for the inspected application.

torch.assessment: Transitive through Docling. No direct torch.jit.script use was found in the application or the inspected Docling wheels. Torch and torchvision must be upgraded as a compatible pair.

transformers.assessment: Transitive through Docling. Inspected callers load processors and models, but do not save_pretrained. The advisory minimum 5.10.0 is yanked; the proposed candidate uses the available non-yanked 5.10.1 release.

supplementary_advisories.assessment: Tracked repository content can impersonate Git metadata. File reads need repository/config access; code execution additionally needs index.commit. Streamlit opens and reads the local checkout; no attacker-controlled checkout or commit path was demonstrated.
Malformed commit author or committer data can exhaust CPU during metadata parsing. Requires an attacker-controlled commit reaching the local GitPython consumer.

A diff option bypass permits a blind file-content oracle. PyPI associates this with 3.1.50, but the maintainer lists only 3.1.59. Counted as an upgrade-path advisory, not a confirmed additional match for the installed version.

metadata_conflicts.resolution: The candidate selects 3.14.3. GitHub compare confirms the advisory fix commit is its ancestor.
Excluded from additional confirmed installed-version matches; included in upgrade review.
No fixed version established. Do not equate absence from a bounded advisory range with a verified fix.

security_probe_sources.probe_accelerate.py:
"""Test checkpoint containment using only tiny synthetic tensors."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile

import accelerate
from accelerate import load_checkpoint_in_model
import torch

root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="accelerate-probe-", dir=Path(__file__).parent))
checkpoint = root / "checkpoint"
outside = root / "outside"
checkpoint.mkdir()
outside.mkdir()
weights = outside / "weights.bin"
torch.save({"weight": torch.tensor([[9.0]]), "bias": torch.tensor([4.0])}, weights)
outcomes = []
for label, shard in [("relative", "../outside/weights.bin"), ("absolute", str(weights))]:
    index = checkpoint / (label + ".index.json")
    index.write_text(json.dumps({"weight_map": {"weight": shard, "bias": shard}}))
    model = torch.nn.Linear(1, 1)
    try:
        load_checkpoint_in_model(model, str(index))
        outcomes.append({"case": label, "outside_tensor_loaded": model.weight.item() == 9.0 and model.bias.item() == 4.0})
    except Exception as error:
        outcomes.append({"case": label, "outside_tensor_loaded": False, "error_type": type(error).__name__, "error": str(error)})
print(json.dumps({"accelerate": accelerate.__version__, "torch": torch.__version__, "outcomes": outcomes, "synthetic_files": str(root)}, sort_keys=True))

limits: The full application was not upgraded or regression-tested against the proposed dependency set.
Accelerate runtime probes timed out at 90 seconds without a result; 1.15.0 was assessed from the verified wheel source.
No production host, container image, or service on another port was inspected. Local lsof found no listener on 8501 or 4200.
The previous passing pytest run used /tmp/bubble-refresh-20260916, which lacks 13 of these 14 packages and uses fixed pydantic-settings 2.15.0.
GitHub CI run 35233070407 on 5ee3af5 failed at Ruff; format, typecheck, and tests were skipped. The separate Pages workflow succeeded.
A global advisory API lookup returned 404 for the three additional GitPython IDs; their public maintainer endpoints were successfully retrieved.
The web fetch of the OpenSSL advisory failed; a direct read of the same official URL succeeded and was saved.
A first GitConfigParser probe used a list where writable mode requires a single filename; that constructor error was corrected before the reported reproduction.
A first targeted resolution chose yanked Transformers 5.10.0. The retained candidate uses non-yanked 5.10.1.
Static call inspection is not proof that every indirect or dynamically selected path is unreachable.
This audit is not a compromise investigation and does not establish whether these vulnerabilities were previously exploited.

source_scan.note: Untracked duplicate files appeared during the audit. The final parse and import scan included them; none were changed.

remediation.status: 53 original alerts patched; Accelerate remains vulnerable upstream and is mitigated at the EDGAR HTML conversion boundary. No alert dismissed.

vulnerabilities.details: Hugging Face Accelerate through 1.14.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in load_checkpoint_in_model and load_checkpoint_and_dispatch functions that fail to sanitize weight_map entries from sharded checkpoint indexes. Attackers can supply relative paths with ../ sequences or absolute paths to read arbitrary files, or point shard entries at named pipes to cause indefinite blocking and denial of service.

Hugging Face Accelerate through 1.14.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in load_checkpoint_in_model and load_checkpoint_and_dispatch functions that fail to sanitize weight_map entries from sharded checkpoint indexes. Attackers can supply relative paths with ../ sequences or absolute paths to read arbitrary files, or point shard entries at named pipes to cause indefinite blocking and denial of service.

mitigation.scope: Both EdgarExtractor converter entry points use the restricted converter. Direct use of Accelerate outside this application boundary is still affected.

verification.mypy_result: Success: no issues found in 142 source files

verification_notes: The first full-suite attempt from a scratch working directory failed three relative-fixture lookups. The repository-root runs passed, ending at 858 tests after adding direct extractor coverage.
A positive form-parser test initially set a limit below the combined field-name and value size. The test now uses an adequate size; the two malicious-limit cases pass.

Copying the old environment and bundling all Git objects blocked on macOS cloud-only files. Both partial snapshots were retained. The complete original environment was preserved by a directory rename, and the Git refs/index were separately saved. No historical Git objects were removed.
The original mypy attempt blocked on a cloud-only cache database. A fresh local cache completed and passed after type corrections and adding lxml-stubs.
The broad historical commit scan matched 136 lines; 130 attribution lines predate this change. Historical commits are preserved. The new commit must contain zero attribution trailers.
No paid model calls or production analytics queries were made. No compromised-host investigation was performed.
